title: Charm caster sequence (Sequence)AB_Charm_Channeling: nothing drawn (not a beam)
summary: The sequence historically catalogued as 'the Charm beam' and still the ctx.Effects.ServerBeamLink default. Live inspection on 2026-09-06 found that the caster buff AB_Charm_Channeling (1002852223) has one BuffSequence row, -389499105, whose asset-reference list holds only mat_Transparent_Weapon01. Played alone through ServerBeamLink, nothing drawn: no beam and no particles. It is not the Charm spell. The Charm presentation belongs to the target debuff's sequence (charm-target-channel-sequence).

requirements.world: server world spawns a NetworkedSequence carrier; every client resolves the hash in its client-only sequence prefab map

context.carrier: NetworkedSequence (651179295) + SpawnSequenceForEntity {SequenceGuid, Target, SecondaryTarget, PlayOnSelf} through ctx.Effects.ServerBeamLink(source, target, seconds: 20f, sequenceGuid: -389499105). The handle is tracked so plugin unload destroys it. Callers without a context use the static ServerBeam.Link(startIndex, startVersion, endIndex, endVersion, seconds, sequenceGuid, owner, pluginId).
context.endpoints: source and target must be networked Unity.Entities.Entity values carrying NetworkId (a character or a spawned unit; a bare marker entity does not replicate). The sequence prefab carries Pull_Entity + Pull_BuffTarget per docs/effects.md.
context.lifetime: Link seconds argument (20 s in the probe)

initialization: ctx.Effects.ServerBeamLink(source, target, seconds: 20f, sequenceGuid: -389499105) on the server. source and target must be networked Unity.Entities.Entity values carrying NetworkId (a character or a spawned unit; a bare marker entity does not replicate). The handle is tracked so plugin unload destroys it. Callers without a context use the static ServerBeam.Link(startIndex, startVersion, endIndex, endVersion, seconds, sequenceGuid, owner, pluginId).
Nothing else: the client resolves and draws whatever the sequence graph does with its asset list.
cleanup: Dispose the ServerBeam handle (observed: 'Effects: server beam disposed').
Client carriers may outlive server disposal: five NetworkedSequence carriers were still present on the client after disposal and were removed by explicit per-entity DestroyUtility calls (E4, E5).

controls.name: endpoints
controls.limitations: Two-entity endpoints are the Link API's contract (docs/effects.md); with this sequence no beam body is referenced, so endpoint tracking of a Charm beam cannot be observed through it.

discovery.note: Buff -> BuffSequence row -> sequence entity -> one asset reference, read live on the client. sides client: sequence/asset enumeration is a client readback.

playback.note: Carrier spawned on the server and mirrored on the client with both endpoints set (2026-09-07 through the Sample's tracked ServerBeam.Link). sides server+client: server spawn plus client mirror.

appearance.note: Reproduced 2026-09-07: no beam and no particles drawn with this sequence, before and after moving the player endpoint. Historical claims that this sequence is the Charm beam are superseded. sides server+client: client presentation of a server-spawned carrier (nothing drawn).

controls.note: The player endpoint was moved by a dash during playback; with nothing drawn there is no tracking to observe. The carrier's Target/SecondaryTarget fields stayed set. sides server+client: endpoint fields on the carrier plus client presentation.

gameplayHits.note: Visual sequence carrier; no gameplay effect is attached by Link. sides server: no gameplay hit is attached.

naturalCleanup.note: The server disposed the carrier at the 20 s deadline; the client's carrier entity survived the server disposal until destroyed explicitly. sides server+client: server deadline disposal plus leftover client carrier.

explicitCleanup.note: Server handle disposal at the deadline is logged. The client carrier did not follow: it was removed by a manual client-side DestroyUtility (a recovery procedure, request logged), and the post-destroy zero-carrier query is agent-reported. Server disposal does not clean the client on its own. sides server+client: server handle disposal plus leftover client carrier.

poolReuse.note: Not examined. sides client: pooling would be a client observation if tested.
